name: Heading-list item continuation
mechanism:
Positions are the next entry in a repeated heading/index template ('#### X

#### Y

#### [[Z]]', map-index lines ending in newline); heads 16.8/16.2 with a6/a7 directions appear to track the repeated list structure and emit the next item or line break.

name: Section-heading sequence continuation
mechanism: Almost all positions complete the next '####' heading or the newline ending a map-index line in a run of parallel headings; a6/a7/a16 directions carry the repeated-heading pattern forward.

name: Listing-line boundary tokens
mechanism: Positions are mostly end-of-line or field-separator tokens (newlines, spaces before hours/tube glyphs, semicolons) inside structured listing blocks plus a few heading continuations; the a7/a16 directions seem to mark where a listing field or line ends.

name: Connective before proper noun
mechanism: The damaged token is almost always a function word or punctuation immediately preceding a named entity (' the Shard', ', Piccadilly', '### Canterbury'); heads 16.3/16.4/16.5 appear to set up the transition into an upcoming proper-noun mention.

name: Index-line termination
mechanism: Positions are newlines ending map-key index lines ('4Tate ModernD1[[\n]]'), section-index labels, and heading-list entries; a7/a16 directions detect the end of one numbered index entry so the next can start.

name: Listing end-of-line newlines
mechanism: Mostly newline (and semicolon) tokens closing lines in listings, indexes, and heading runs; the same a7/a16 subspace as its siblings, here handling the line-break decision itself.

name: Boilerplate label completion
mechanism: Positions complete recurring template words split across tokens in index/listing scaffolding ('Enter[[tainment]]', 'Sh[[opping]]', 'GOOGLE[[ MAP]]', 'TOURIST[[ INFORMATION]]'); a6/a7 directions appear to copy the stereotyped section-label vocabulary.

name: Memorized multi-token phrase continuation
mechanism: A very large, loose root whose common thread is continuing multi-token names and boilerplate mid-word ('Le]]icester', 'Broad[[casting]] House', 'Lamb &[[ Flag]]', 'Sle[[eping]]'); attention layer 9 plus heads 6.3/6.7/9.8 look like general copy/induction machinery, but the set is heterogeneous.

name: Listing contact-field tokens
mechanism: Positions sit inside formulaic contact/detail fields of venue listings - postcode fragments ('NW[[1]]', '[[ N]]6'), 'adult/[[child]]', street numbers, phone digits, '8[[Information]]'; a9 directions with heads 9.0/9.7/9.8 supply the listing-field format.

name: Adult/child and postcode fields
mechanism: Dominated by the 'adult/[[child]]' price template and London postcode digits ('NW[[1]]', 'SE[[1]]') in listing address lines; a9 directions complete these highly stereotyped ticket-price and postcode formats.

name: Listing header boundaries
mechanism: A mixed set of closing parens after URLs, newlines in name indexes, and venue-name continuations; plausibly the boundary tokens of listing header lines, but the common function is diffuse.

name: Priced-item noun before amount
mechanism: The damaged token is usually the noun naming what a following pound-price applies to ('[[ steak]] £20', 'tap[[as]] £5', '[[ tacos]] £5', 'four[[ courses]] £28', 'adult/[[child]] £5'); a9 directions appear to predict the unit-being-priced slot in listing price fields.

name: URL and postcode suffixes
mechanism: Positions are domain-suffix tokens in listing URLs ('www.nhm[[.]]ac', '.[[org]].uk') and postcode district tokens ('[[ SE]]1', '[[ N]]6'), plus adult/child fields; a9 directions complete these fixed address-format suffixes.

name: Listing shorthand completion
mechanism: A loose mix of split-word name/heading continuations ('Marg[[ate]]', 'P[[ARK]]') and single-letter room-rate abbreviations before prices ('s/[[d]] £110', '[[ r]] £70'); reads as general completion of listing shorthand, but no single tight function.

name: Room-rate abbreviation fields
mechanism: Many positions are the compressed room-price tokens of accommodation listings ('d[[ from]] £135', 's/[[d]] £110', '[[ r]] £70', 'ste[[ from]] £90') mixed with proper-name continuations; a9 directions seem to handle the rate-field shorthand before pound amounts.

name: Adult/child fields and index breaks
mechanism: Combines the 'adult/[[child]]' ticket-price template with newlines ending section-index lines ('5Eating[[\n]]'); the same a9 subspace as its siblings, applied to these two stereotyped listing slots.

name: All-caps category-tag completion
mechanism: Positions complete the all-caps venue category tag appended to a name ('FER[[RY]]', 'STAD[[IUM]]', 'MUSE[[UM]]', 'MEX[[ICAN]]', 'CLOTH[[ING]]') and related section labels; a6 directions with heads 9.4/9.8 finish the fixed category-tag vocabulary.
